surface_summary: The old pawnbroker Daniel Multenius is found dead in his shop, apparently assaulted. Suspicion falls on Andrew Lauriston, a young lodger who was found with rings similar to those in the shop. A complex investigation reveals a stolen valuable diamond and a series of murders involving Chinese tenants and a Japanese medical student.
accepted_facts: Daniel Multenius was found dead in his pawnshop parlour.
Two rings similar to those in the pawnshop tray were found in Lauriston's possession.
A rare orange-yellow diamond worth eighty thousand pounds was sent to Multenius.
Chen Li, one of the Chinese tenants, was found murdered in Molteno Lodge.
inferred_conclusions: Lauriston stole the rings and murdered Multenius.
Levendale lost the rare book in a bus as he claimed.
Chang Li was the murderer of Chen Li.
mechanism_description: Mori Yada, a Japanese medical student, stole the orange-yellow diamond and banknotes from Daniel Multenius. He hid the diamond in the pigtail of Chen Li, one of the Chinese tenants, whom he later murdered to cover his crime. Yada attempted to escape but was caught by Melky Rubinstein, recovering the stolen property and clearing Lauriston of suspicion.
delivery_path: Yada steals the diamond and banknotes from Multenius's parlour.
He hides the diamond in Chen Li's pigtail.
Chen Li is murdered by Yada to conceal the theft.
Yada uses the detective's card to access the mortuary and retrieve the diamond.
Yada attempts to escape with the diamond and money.
Melky Rubinstein tricks Yada into a locked room and recovers the stolen items.
Yada is arrested after his escape attempt fails.
outcome_result: Mori Yada is exposed as the thief and murderer, and the stolen diamond and money are recovered.

false_assumption.statement: Andrew Lauriston stole the rings and murdered Daniel Multenius.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Lauriston was found alone at the crime scene with rings similar to those in the pawnshop tray, and he was financially desperate. The police and public naturally suspect him given these facts.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the involvement of Mori Yada, who committed the theft and murder while framing Lauriston by exploiting the similarity of the rings and Lauriston's presence.

supporting_points: Lauriston was found alone with the dead pawnbroker.
He possessed rings similar to those in the pawnshop tray.
He was financially desperate and had pawned his watch and rings.
His behavior was nervous and suspicious.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: No direct evidence links Lauriston to the murder, and the rings were proven to be legitimately his through later testimony and expert examination.

red_herrings.description: Chang Li, one of the Chinese tenants, is suspected of murder and theft due to his disappearance and connection to the pawnshop.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Chang Li's absence and proximity to the crime scene.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Chang Li was in an opium stupor and later found murdered himself, making him a victim rather than a culprit.

red_herrings.description: Spencer Levendale's disappearance and disguise as a tramp raise suspicion about his involvement.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Levendale's secret dealings, disappearance, and possession of chloroform.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Levendale was searching for the stolen diamond and money alongside Stephen Purvis and was not involved in the murder.

closed_circle.rationale: The suspects are limited to those with access to the pawnshop and knowledge of the diamond theft and murder: Lauriston (present at the scene), Levendale (business partner with secret dealings), Chang Li (tenant and missing), and Yada (tenant and thief).

time_windows: Night of November 19th (Parslett's poisoning and Chen Li's murder)

Testimony of Mr. Edward Killick identifying rings as given to Lauriston's mother

inference_path.correction: Levendale did not lose the book in a bus but brought it himself
inference_path.effect: Levendale's story about the book is suspicious

inference_path.correction: Parslett was poisoned by the murderer to silence him
inference_path.effect: Murderer is an expert in poisons and local

Medical expert testimony on poison and symptoms

inference_path.observation: Chen Li found murdered in Molteno Lodge
inference_path.correction: Chen Li was murdered by Mori Yada to cover theft
inference_path.effect: Yada is implicated in murder and theft

Yada's possession of platinum solitaire studs matching those found

inference_path.observation: Yada visited mortuary alone with detective's card
inference_path.correction: Yada used the card to access Chen Li's body and retrieve the hidden diamond
required_evidence: Mortuary keeper's testimony about Yada's visit
Dr. Mirandolet's observation of diamond hidden in pigtail

inference_path.observation: Yada escapes after being locked in a room by Melky
inference_path.correction: Yada's escape attempt fails and he is recaptured with stolen items
inference_path.effect: Culprit apprehended and stolen property recovered
required_evidence: Melky Rubinstein's testimony of tricking Yada
Recovery of diamond and banknotes from Yada's possession

inference_path.observation: Levendale and Purvis disappear and reappear disguised
inference_path.correction: They were searching for the stolen diamond and money and were not involved in the murder
inference_path.effect: Levendale and Purvis are cleared of suspicion
required_evidence: Levendale's confession and explanation to police
John Purvis's testimony about his brother and diamond

discriminating_test.design: Police and associates conduct a raid on Pilmansey's Tea Rooms at midday when the opium den is active. They enter as customers with plain-clothes officers, close the place, and insist on being shown the opium den. The presence of Chang Li there will confirm the location of the thief and stolen property.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The raid reveals the hiding place of Chang Li, who possesses the stolen diamond and money, confirming the location of the stolen goods and implicating the thief.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Successful identification and capture of Chang Li in the opium den during the raid.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of characters, their movements, and possessions such as the rings and the platinum solitaire studs. The significance of the marks on the rings and the presence of the studs are highlighted. The narrative provides clues about the diamond's theft, the murder of Chen Li, and Yada's suspicious behavior. The reader could have deduced Yada's guilt by connecting the theft, the murder, and the unique platinum studs found at multiple locations.
